items.pronunciation_notes: लगता is two even beats, lag-taa, with the length only on the second.
items.gloss_en: I think — literally, to me it seems

learn.title_en: The same verb, now with no noun at all
learn.explanation_en: So far लगना has been carrying nouns — भूख, डर, ठंड. Here it carries a whole thought instead, and मुझे लगता है means "it seems to me", which in ordinary use is simply "I think". There is no noun for the verb to agree with, so it falls back to masculine singular: लगता है, always, for every speaker. That default is worth naming, because it is the same neutral form you met in Module 9 when को blocked agreement. When Hindi has nothing to agree with, it uses the masculine singular. What follows is usually कि and the thought itself.

literal_vs_natural.hindi: मुझे लगता है कि वह आएगा।
literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me it seems that he will come.

examples.hindi: मुझे लगता है कि वह आएगा।
examples.read_as: mujhe lagtaa hai ki vah aaegaa.
examples.note: कि introduces the thought.

examples.hindi: मुझे लगता है कि यह सही है।
examples.read_as: mujhe lagtaa hai ki yah sahii hai.
examples.note: लगता है never changes, whoever is speaking.
The question form — extremely common in conversation.

common_error.why_en: मैं लगता हूँ means "I seem" — a sentence about how you appear to others, not about what you think.

practice.question: ___ लगता है कि वह आएगा।
practice.explanation_en: The thought arrives at a person, so the person is marked with को.

game.explanation_en: मुझे लगता है. The first means "I seem", and the third invents a feminine form where there is nothing to agree with.

tts_strings: मुझे लगता है कि वह आएगा।
मुझे लगता है कि यह सही है।

items.pronunciation_notes: ऐ is a single vowel close to the one in English 'air': ai-saa.
items.gloss_en: I get the feeling — a softened opinion

learn.explanation_en: ऐसा means "such, like this", and dropping it into the sentence softens what follows: मुझे ऐसा लगता है is closer to "I get the feeling" than to "I think". It is what you use when you are not certain, or when you are disagreeing politely — which in Hindi conversation is most of the time. ऐसा stays masculine singular throughout, because it is pointing at a thought rather than at any noun, and thoughts have no gender.

examples.note: Softer than मुझे लगता है on its own.
The auxiliary drops after नहीं, as it usually does.

examples.hindi: मुझे ऐसा लगता है कि वह नहीं आएगा।
examples.read_as: mujhe aisaa lagtaa hai ki vah nahiiṁ aaegaa.
examples.english: I have a feeling he won't come.
examples.note: ऐसा and कि together — the thought is stated and hedged at once.

common_error.why_en: There is no noun in the sentence to agree with, so both words stay masculine singular.

practice.question: ___ ऐसा नहीं लगता।
practice.explanation_en: वह goes oblique and fuses with को to give उसे.

game.explanation_en: Masculine singular throughout, because nothing in the sentence has gender.

tts_strings: मुझे ऐसा लगता है कि वह नहीं आएगा।

items.pronunciation_notes: Two beats with the length on the second: la-gaa.
items.gloss_en: I thought — and usually, I was wrong

learn.title_en: The past, and what it quietly implies
learn.explanation_en: मुझे लगा is the perfective: "it seemed to me", "I thought". In practice it usually carries the implication that you turned out to be wrong — मुझे लगा कि तुम आओगे is close to "I thought you'd come", said to somebody who did not. Notice there is no ने anywhere in it. लगना is intransitive, so Module 9 never applies, and the experiencer marking stays exactly as it was in the present. That combination — perfective, no ने, dative subject — is worth seeing once, because it is where the two modules meet without conflicting.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me it seemed that you would come.

examples.note: And the implication is that you did not.

examples.english: That's how it seemed to me.
examples.note: Perfective of the softened form.

examples.hindi: उसे लगा कि यह सही है।
examples.read_as: use lagaa ki yah sahii hai.
examples.note: Different experiencer, identical verb.

common_error.why_en: लगना is intransitive and never takes ने. The person is an experiencer, not an agent.

practice.question: ___ लगा कि तुम आओगे।
practice.explanation_en: The dative stays in the perfective. लगना takes no ने.

game.explanation_en: मुझे लगा. ने cannot appear with लगना, and there is nothing feminine for लगी to agree with.

tts_strings: उसे लगा कि यह सही है।

summary.recap_en: मुझे लगता है is लगना carrying a thought rather than a noun, so it defaults to masculine singular and never changes. ऐसा softens it. मुझे लगा is the past, usually implying you were mistaken — and it takes no ने, because लगना is intransitive.
summary.next_up_en: Next: चाहिए — the one construction here where nothing agrees with anything.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three beats: chaa-hi-e, with the length on the first and a light glide off the end.
items.gloss_en: I need water — literally, to me water is wanted

learn.title_en: चाहिए never changes for the person
learn.explanation_en: चाहिए means "is wanted, is needed", so मुझे पानी चाहिए is literally "to me water is wanted". The thing needed is the subject and the person is the destination — the same shape as पसंद. What makes चाहिए easy is that it has no person forms at all: मुझे चाहिए, तुम्हें चाहिए, उन्हें चाहिए, आपको चाहिए. One word, no conjugation, nothing to get wrong. Do not confuse it with चाहना, which is an ordinary verb — मैं पानी चाहता हूँ is grammatical but sounds forceful and stilted where चाहिए would be natural.

examples.note: पानी is the subject.
The form you will be asked in every shop.
मदद is feminine and चाहिए still does not move.

common_error.why_en: The person is the destination, not the subject. पानी is what the sentence is about.

practice.question: ___ पानी चाहिए।
practice.explanation_en: चाहिए takes an experiencer, so मुझे.

game.explanation_en: मुझे पानी चाहिए. चाहिए is complete on its own and takes no auxiliary behind it.

items.gloss_en: I should go — चाहिए with an infinitive

learn.title_en: An infinitive in front turns need into should
learn.explanation_en: Put an infinitive before चाहिए and it stops meaning "need a thing" and starts meaning "ought to": मुझे जाना चाहिए, I should go. Literally, "to me going is wanted". Infinitives are masculine singular as always, so nothing moves anywhere. This is how Hindi expresses obligation and advice, and it is far commoner than any of the alternatives — if you want to tell someone they should rest, this is the sentence. For "should have", add था: मुझे जाना चाहिए था.

examples.note: Infinitive plus चाहिए.
A करना verb as the infinitive — the pattern takes any of them.
था turns advice into regret.

common_error.why_en: Obligation lands on a person, and a person something lands on is marked with को.

practice.question: ___ आराम करना चाहिए।
practice.explanation_en: चाहिए takes an experiencer, so तुम goes to तुम्हें.

game.explanation_en: The infinitive जाना, then चाहिए, with the person in the dative.

items.gloss_en: I need two books — and चाहिए still holds still

learn.title_en: Plural things, and चाहिए does not budge
learn.explanation_en: Compare पसंद, where a plural thing forced हैं. चाहिए does not do that. मुझे दो किताबें चाहिए is the everyday form and it is invariant. A plural चाहिएँ does exist and turns up in careful writing, but it is formal, optional, and not what people say. So चाहिए is the one construction in this module where nothing agrees with anything at all — no gender, no number, no person. After four levels of endings moving around, that is a genuine rest.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me two books are wanted.

examples.note: Plural thing, and the verb is unchanged.
The negative sits in front and चाहिए still holds.
Different experiencer, same flat verb.

common_error.why_en: चाहिए is complete in itself and does not take a form of होना behind it.

practice.question: ___ और समय चाहिए।
practice.explanation_en: हमें for the experiencer. हमने is the ergative form and belongs to Module 9.

game.explanation_en: चाहिए stands alone. Adding हैं or हूँ behind it is the commonest slip here.

summary.recap_en: चाहिए means "is wanted" and never changes — not for person, not for gender, not for number. A thing in front of it means need; an infinitive in front of it means should. Adding है or हैं behind it is the one thing to avoid.
summary.next_up_en: Next: लगना without any experiencer at all — three more jobs for the same verb.

items.pronunciation_notes: बीमार has the length on the first syllable and again on the second: bii-maar.
items.gloss_en: he seems ill — लगना with no dative at all

learn.title_en: Take the experiencer away and the rule reverses
learn.explanation_en: Drop the dative and लगना simply means "to seem". वह बीमार लगता है — he seems ill. And now the person is the subject, so the verb agrees with them: वह बीमार लगती है for a woman. After twelve levels of "the person never controls the verb", that reversal is startling, and it is worth being precise about why. The rule was never about people. It was about experiencers. No experiencer, no blocking. Put one back and the old behaviour returns immediately: मुझे वह बीमार लगता है, he seems ill to me.

examples.note: No dative. The verb agrees with वह.
Feminine subject, feminine verb — impossible in any earlier level of this module.
Add the experiencer back and it stops controlling anything again.

common_error.why_en: उसे would make him the experiencer, so the sentence would mean something seems ill to him — a different claim entirely.

practice.question: ___ बीमार लगता है।
practice.explanation_en: There is no experiencer in this meaning, so the person is a plain subject: वह.

game.explanation_en: वह बीमार लगता है. The last option is grammatical but says she looks ill.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both nouns have the length on the second syllable: dii-vaar, tas-viir.
items.gloss_en: there's a picture on the wall — लगना as attached

learn.title_en: लगना as attached, mounted, put up
learn.explanation_en: Third meaning: to be attached or fixed to something. दीवार पर तस्वीर लगी है — a picture is up on the wall. तस्वीर is feminine, so लगी. There is no experiencer and no dative; there is an ordinary subject and a place marked with पर. This meaning is behind a great deal of everyday Hindi that has nothing to do with feelings — ताला लगा है, the lock is on; लाइन लगी है, there's a queue. If you see लगना with पर and a place, this is the meaning.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: On the wall a picture is attached.
literal_vs_natural.natural_en: There's a picture on the wall.

examples.english: There's a picture on the wall.
examples.note: तस्वीर is feminine and it is the subject.
ताला is masculine, so लगा. दरवाज़ा goes oblique before पर.
The same verb, and nothing is attached to anything physically.

common_error.why_en: तस्वीर is feminine and it is the subject of the sentence.

practice.question: दीवार पर ___ लगी है।
practice.explanation_en: The picture is the plain subject — no को, no ने, and singular to match लगी है.

game.explanation_en: तस्वीर is feminine singular, and the place takes पर rather than को.

items.pronunciation_notes: घ is an aspirated g and ट is retroflex: ghan-ṭe.
items.gloss_en: it takes two hours — लगना as cost or take

learn.explanation_en: Fourth meaning: to be spent, to be taken. दो घंटे लगते हैं — two hours are taken, meaning it takes two hours. घंटे is masculine plural, so लगते हैं. The same verb covers money: सौ रुपये लगते हैं, it costs a hundred rupees. And the person for whom it takes that long can come back in the dative: मुझे दो घंटे लगते हैं, it takes me two hours. So this meaning sits on the boundary between the two halves of the module — it works with an experiencer or without one, and the verb follows the quantity either way.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me two hours are applied.

examples.note: घंटे is masculine plural, so लगते हैं.
The dative is added and the verb does not move.
Money behaves exactly like time here.

common_error.why_en: घंटे is masculine plural, so both the verb and the auxiliary are plural.

practice.question: ___ दो घंटे लगते हैं।
practice.explanation_en: The person it takes that long for is an experiencer, so मुझे.

game.explanation_en: घंटे is masculine plural, so लगते हैं.

summary.recap_en: Without an experiencer, लगना means to seem, to be attached, or to cost. In all three the person or thing in front is an ordinary subject and the verb agrees with it — because the blocking rule was never about people, it was about experiencers.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last meaning, and all five side by side.

levels.title_en: Beginning, being struck, and the whole picture

items.pronunciation_notes: रोने is two beats, ro-ne, with the oblique -ने ending short.
items.gloss_en: he began to cry — लगना as begin

learn.title_en: An oblique infinitive means something started
learn.explanation_en: Fifth meaning: to begin. The recipe is an oblique infinitive plus लगना — रोना becomes रोने, then लगा. वह रोने लगा, he started crying. That oblique ending is Module 6 doing one more job: an infinitive standing in front of another element goes to -ने, exactly as a noun would. There is no dative and no experiencer here, so the person is an ordinary subject and the verb agrees with them: वह रोने लगी for a woman. The construction always implies a sudden start rather than a gradual one.

examples.note: Oblique infinitive रोने, then लगा agreeing with वह.
Feminine subject, feminine verb.
बारिश is feminine, and it is the subject.

common_error.why_en: The infinitive must go oblique to -ने before लगना. रोना is the direct form and cannot stand there.

practice.question: ___ रोने लगा।
practice.explanation_en: The beginning meaning has no experiencer, so the person is a plain subject.

game.explanation_en: Oblique रोने, plain subject वह, and no ने anywhere — लगना is intransitive.

items.pronunciation_notes: ट is retroflex and closes the syllable: choṭ, one beat.
items.gloss_en: I got hurt — literally, an injury was applied to me

learn.explanation_en: चोट means injury, and चोट लगना is to be struck by one: मुझे चोट लगी, literally an injury was applied to me. चोट is feminine, so लगी. This closes the circle. After three meanings with no experiencer at all, the dative returns — and it returns for exactly the reason it appeared in level one: something has happened to a person who did not choose it. If you want to say where, use में on the body part: मुझे पैर में चोट लगी.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me an injury was applied.

examples.note: चोट is feminine, so लगी.
Noun experiencer, oblique plus को.
The body part takes में, not a possessive.

common_error.why_en: लगना is intransitive and takes no ने, and the person is an experiencer rather than an agent.

practice.question: ___ चोट लगी।
practice.explanation_en: Oblique बच्चे, then को as a separate word.

game.explanation_en: मुझे for the experiencer, लगी for feminine चोट, and no ने anywhere.

items.gloss_en: the five meanings of लगना, side by side

learn.title_en: One verb, five jobs, and the sentence tells you which
learn.explanation_en: लगना is among the hardest-working verbs in Hindi, and the five uses are worth seeing together — because what distinguishes them is never the verb, it is the shape of the sentence around it. Felt: मुझे भूख लगी है, with a dative in front. Seem: वह बीमार लगता है, with an ordinary subject and no dative. Attached: दीवार पर तस्वीर लगी है, with पर and a place. Cost or take: दो घंटे लगते हैं, with a quantity as the subject. Begin: वह रोने लगा, with an oblique infinitive in front. A dative means a sensation, an oblique infinitive means a beginning, पर and a place means attachment. That is why this module taught लगना through its constructions rather than as five dictionary entries to memorise.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me two hours are applied.

examples.note: Dative in front — the sensation meaning.
No dative — the seeming meaning.
Oblique infinitive — the beginning meaning.

common_error.why_en: The beginning meaning has no experiencer at all, so the person is an ordinary subject.

practice.question: ___ पैर में चोट लगी।
practice.explanation_en: Being hurt is something that happens to a person, so the experiencer form उसे.

game.explanation_en: The beginning meaning takes a plain subject. The last option is grammatical but means something seems ill to me.

summary.recap_en: An oblique infinitive plus लगना means something began — वह रोने लगा. चोट लगना brings the dative back for the last time. And the five meanings are told apart by the sentence around the verb, not by the verb: a dative means felt, no dative means seem, पर means attached, a quantity means cost, an oblique infinitive means begin.
